AUTHOR: Mandal
TITLE: Assessing fish abundance from underwater video using deep neural networks
REGION: Southeast Queensland, Australia (surf beaches and estuaries, e.g. Coolum, Currimundi)
SPECIES: 50 fish and crustacean species (e.g. mackerel tuna, school mackerel, sand whiting, southern herring, blue swimmer crab, stingarees, rays)
DATA: Own RUVS footage (baited and unbaited GoPro) from University of Sunshine Coast / Griffith collaboration; 4909 annotated frames
D_EV: Sec. IV Dataset: 'The dataset was divided into training, validation, and test sets using a random sampling technique. The training, validation and test set comprises of 70%, 10%, and 20%'
R_EV: Sec. IV: '4909 images containing 12365 annotated samples of 50 species of fish and crustaceans were used in our experiments' (single own dataset, random split)
C_EV: no statement found (only IoU > 50% criterion stated; confidence threshold not reported)
E_EV: Table II / Sec. IV: 'maximum mAP of 82.4% was achieved on the VGG16 network' (AP/mAP only, no abundance output evaluated)
ARCH: Faster R-CNN (RPN) with ZF, CNN-M and VGG-16 backbones, Caffe
METR: Per-class AP, mAP (0.72 all species; 0.824 on well-sampled species subset), inference time (5-10 fps)
NOTE: Water turbidity and illumination are mentioned only as generic challenges in the Introduction, not characterised for the data; coded V1 = NR. Platform: 'baited and unbaited GoPro cameras' (RUVS) - coded BRUV but mixed baited/unbaited. Frame-level random split; frames from the same videos likely in train and test, no leakage discussion. Qualitative error analysis (occlusion, false positives on background surf) exists but no FP rate. Experiment II restricts to species with adequate training samples. Title mentions abundance but no abundance metric is produced or validated.
